item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00162","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C13","C25","C15"],"selected_candidate_label":"C13","confidence":0.86,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C13 plausibly supplied a material argumentative template: identify an imminent Senate vote on a reorganization plan, explain the administrative defect the plan corrects, answer opponents by showing that they previously supported substantially the same mechanism in substitute legislation, characterize the remaining opposition as political rather than merits-based, and close by urging Senate approval. The child adapts this distinctive sequence to the Bureau of Internal Revenue and makes the prior-substitute inconsistency its central argument. C25 is also a strong broader template for defending reorganization plans through Hoover Commission support, efficiency-and-economy claims, rebuttal of objections, and a test-of-political-sincerity framing. C15 concerns the identical plan but is too short and close in time to contribute more than a limited opening formulation and summary claim.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Since that is the only real difference, it is clear that those who support the \"substitute\" bill also support all of my reorganization plan except the part which eliminates political patronage","parent_excerpt":"Last year, the Senate passed a bill, commonly known as the Taft-Smith-Donnell substitute... Among the provisions which that bill contained... was one to abolish the office of the Independent General Counsel... That is exactly the object of plan twelve.","explanation":"Both expose opposition to a reorganization plan as inconsistent by demonstrating that opponents had supported substantially the same administrative change in substitute legislation."},{"child_excerpt":"those who find it to their advantage to preserve the present system, or to play politics... have raised specious arguments against the plan that obscure the real issue","parent_excerpt":"most of the opponents of plan twelve are more concerned with politics than with the merits of the proposal","explanation":"The same political-versus-merits framing supports the substitute-legislation comparison."},{"child_excerpt":"The plain fact is that the plan must stand or fall on one issue","parent_excerpt":"The issues now involved in consideration of plan twelve are not matters of personalities...","explanation":"Each narrows the controversy to the true administrative issue after dismissing opponents' framing."},{"child_excerpt":"The Hoover Commission on Reorganization of the Executive Branch of the Government has taken that position.","parent_excerpt":"Two of its important recommendations are included in Reorganization Plans No. 1 and No. 2.","explanation":"C25 supplies the broader recurrent machinery of invoking the Hoover Commission as authoritative support for a contested reorganization plan."},{"child_excerpt":"The vote on Reorganization Plan No. will show who it is that is just talking about corruption and who it is that really wants to do something about it.","parent_excerpt":"The action taken on these plans will demonstrate whether the many recent professions of support for increased efficiency and economy in Government are to be taken seriously or are to be written off as political oratory.","explanation":"C25 closely parallels the child's presentation of the Senate vote as a test of whether stated reform commitments are sincere."}]}
